data.acquisitionSummary: Current Three Ireland provider terms and provider-moderated help agree that a prepay number can be terminated for extended inactivity, but the current guidance is internally inconsistent on the safe timing: a 2026 help article describes an alert after at least 90 days plus another 180 days before removal, while other Three guidance says to top up at least every 6 months and the General Terms permit restriction/termination after 12 months without top-up or chargeable use. Credit expiry is a separate rule. The legacy “one SMS every ~80 days” recommendation therefore overstates certainty.

keep.action: Three consistently says a top-up or credit-reducing call/text/data resets dormancy, but current provider guidance conflicts on the relevant inactivity threshold (90+180 days, six-month advice, and a 12-month contractual termination threshold). Do not publish a single cheapest cadence until Three reconciles these rules.

data.chinaActivation: Three Prepay SIM/eSIM is an Irish consumer product. Online/self-service top-up exists, but a reliable China-first acquisition/activation path is not established in this packet.
data.kyc: No evidence in the current Three consumer prepay flow establishes a mandatory national real-name registration regime; acquisition/activation still remains Ireland-centered for this use case.
data.payment: My3 supports top-up and scheduled top-up; current keep-cost is not modeled because lifecycle timing is internally inconsistent.
data.wifiCalling: Not relied on for this route decision.
data.roamingSms: Three provider-moderated support confirms that while abroad the phone can connect automatically to a roaming network and receive calls/texts without enabling mobile-data roaming; exact OTP reliability outside the EU is not independently established.
data.refund: Not relied on for this route decision.
data.holdReason: Current Three provider guidance conflicts on the dormancy timeline, so the prior €0.30/year / 80-day recommendation is not decision-safe. Keep as HOLD until one current lifecycle rule can be reconciled.
data.tariffSummary: HOLD: top-up or chargeable use preserves activity, but current Three materials conflict on 90+180 days vs six-month advice vs 12-month contractual threshold.
guideSteps: HOLD: do not use the legacy 1-SMS/80-day cost model.
Wait for one current provider lifecycle rule before promotion.
